title: MSF ‘outraged’ as two workers killed in Israeli strike on Gaza | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Two Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) workers were killed on Friday in an Israeli strike on a Gaza clinic, the organization said Saturday, sparking outrage amid an escalating Israeli campaign targeting Hamas in the territory.

The workers, who died in a “direct strike,” worked as watchmen at the site, MSF said, adding that the organization is “devastated and outraged.”

Their deaths bring the total number of MSF workers killed during the conflict in Gaza to 17 that began in the wake of the Hamas-led October 7 attacks in 2023, the organization said.

“Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military,” the statement read. “We stand in solidarity with the families and loved ones of our colleagues. We call for accountability.”

World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said “attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable.”

“These attacks MUST STOP,” he wrote on X.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that the strikes targeted two terrorists whothey claimed worked as security guards at the MSF clinic, and denied directly striking medical infrastructure.

“This is another example of the Hamas terrorist organization embedding itself within international organizations,” the IDF said, adding that “contrary to reports, the strike was not directed at a hospital, and no damage was caused to medical infrastructure in the area.”

The Israeli military also said that it took “precautionary measures” to minimize the strike’s harm to civilians.

The attack comes amid intensified Israeli strikes seeking to eliminate Hamas targets in Gaza. On Friday, Hamas accused Israel of attempting to assassinate the son of the Hamas Chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family.

Reuters later cited senior Hamas official Basem Naim as saying that Khalil al-Hayya’s son, Izzeldeen al-Hayya, survived the Friday attack.

There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military.

In recent weeks, Israel intensified its campaign of targeted assassinations in Gaza, striking and killing Hamas commanders and political leaders, as the Trump administration urges Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to proceed with the US-brokered ceasefire plan.

Since the nominal ceasefire was signed more than a year ago, Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza to target Hamas. The Israeli military has claimed that each attack was a “blow” to Hamas’ leadership capabilities, even as the militant organization has firmly entrenched its power in the half of Gaza not occupied by the Israeli military.

Meanwhile, the territory’s Hamas-run health ministry has continued to report mounting causality figures. More than 1,700 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, the ministry said, with more than 6,000 wounded.

CNN’s Nadeen Ebrahim contributed reporting.
